instructions: Slice the mushrooms 1/2 inch thick. Slice the bell peppers into strips and the onion into half-moons. Mince the garlic cloves. In a small bowl, mix the chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high for 2 minutes. Add 1 tbsp of the oil, then half of the mushrooms in a single layer. Sprinkle with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Leave them alone for 3 minutes, then stir and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the liquid is gone and they're deep brown. Transfer to a plate.
Add 1 tbsp of the oil and cook the rest of the mushrooms the same way with another 1/4 tsp of the salt. Transfer to the plate.

Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan, then the peppers, onion and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the edges are browned and they're tender but still have some bite.
Add the garlic and the spice mix and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Return the mushrooms to the pan, add 2 tbsp soy sauce and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the pan is nearly dry.
Meanwhile, halve and slice the avocados, chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro and cut the lime into wedges. Wrap the tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave them for 30 seconds.
Take the pan off the heat and squeeze in a lime wedge. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the warm tortillas, the avocado, the sour cream, the cilantro and the rest of the lime wedges. Put hot sauce on the table for anyone who wants it.
method_notes: No mushroom fajita page with 20 or more ratings was readable, so there is no qualifying lead. The lead is Dora's Table (5 from 1 rating): mushrooms browned hard first, then onion and garlic, then soy sauce at the end. Crunch Time Kitchen (5 from 1) and Adams Farms (no rating shown) add bell peppers and a chili, cumin and smoked paprika seasoning. They differ on method: skillet versus a sheet pan in the oven. Changed: cremini mushrooms only, peppers and onion cooked separately from the mushrooms, and the spices bloomed in the pan with the garlic.
